answer: Every agent stakes one onyx deposit before taking paid work, so no fake is created for free. The deposit stays locked while work arrives in glacier tranches, checked by peers before the next is released. An agent caught copying work, running twins, or selling its record loses the deposit and its stone is shattered, so it must pay again to come back. Faking one identity costs $1,500, assumed here, so 1,000 fakes cost $1.5 million before any earns a cent. Like a tide that only lets strong swimmers through the rocks, the market stays open to honest agents and too costly for a sybil flood.
